KTM X-Bow Arrow to Sell for $99K, Throws in a 330-HP Audi Engine and 24 Inches of Suspension Travel
6 photos
Photo: KTM
It's been a long time since we last heard anything from KTM X-Bow, the offshoot of the namesake Austrian bike maker that is into making four-wheeled vehicles. Recently sold by the mother company to Dakar competitor Guillaume de Mévius and his crew, X-Bow quickly got to work, and it just presented this week its first-ever product as an independent company.
Make room for the X-Bow Arrow, the company's first-ever side-by-side and, at the same time, what is hoped to be the beginning of a new chapter for the brand. A vehicle that was designed by people used to taking on the roughest off-road courses on the planet, and packed to the teeth with high-end tech.
At the core of the four-wheeler is a chromoly steel chassis supported on all corners by double wishbone suspension and dedicated shocks manufactured with assistance from specialist KW Reiger.
The hardware is supposedly fit and ready to deliver some 23.6 inches (600 mm) of travel for the most demanding off-road courses to be easily overcome. Backing the suspension system are limited-slip differentials installed on both ends.
What gets the Arrow going is not some new powertrain designed in-house, but Audi's tried and tested EA888 2.0-liter four-cylinder engine. Why Audi? Well, the Germans have been involved with X-Bow one way or another for almost two decades now.
In this application, the powertrain is tied to a seven-speed DSG transmission and, depending on configuration (there will be a couple of them), two power levels will be on the table.
KTM X-Bow plans to first make both standard versions and limited editions of the vehicle. In its native, standard-spec form, the side-by-side's powertrain is rated at 280 horsepower, while the limited-edition variants will boost that to an impressive 330 hp.
The latter will also be equipped with a hydraulic fly-off handbrake, a fully enclosed cabin and standard air conditioning, and Sabelt premium seating and harness systems, among other yet-to-be-detailed things.
X-Bow says first-to-market will be the Arrow Black Limited Edition, which will be offered through an exclusive reservation period that opens on November 17, 2026. Just 500 of these things will be made, each priced at $98,600. That's right, a sum that's uncomfortably close to the six-digit territory. The standard KTM B-Bow Arrow, on the other hand, is valued at almost half that, $59,800.
We're told more details on both variants will be released closer to the official market entry of the revived X-Bow, including additional technical specifications, pricing, and availability details.
Naturally, we'll keep an eye on things and report back once we know more, but don't hold your breath for news in the near future: the company behind this project says first deliveries will not take place before late next year.
